title: Case: Bookcase ordered for a chosen Thursday keeps going out for delivery earlier in the week
context: A Wrenfield Goods bookcase was ordered with the merchant's pick-your-day option. The recipient is working away from home for part of the week and has written to the desk several times.
initial_request: Morning. Guess what is 'out for delivery today'. It's WEDNESDAY. I am in a hotel 140 miles away until tonight, which, again, is the entire reason I paid for pick your day and picked Thursday. Colm's at his daughter's today so there isn't even anybody to wave at the poor driver. I've picked Thursday on three texts now, three! And I've just read the small print at the bottom of this one which says after three goes it gets sent back?? So it'll be on its way back to the warehouse on the one day this week I'm actually standing in my own hall. Please can someone make Thursday mean Thursday. Sorry for the essay. The lamp really is nice though.

events.to: Quillon Larkham, recipient; Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Thanks for your order TG-1750! Item: Alderby 5-shelf bookcase (2 boxes). Delivery option: Pick Your Day - Thursday 9 September. Carrier: Calloway Arc Logistics, DL-8982. WEEKEND OFFER: 15% off all garden furniture with code PATIO15 until Sunday midnight. Love your order? Tag us for a chance to win a GBP 50 voucher. You are receiving this email because you placed an order with Wrenfield Goods.

Hi! Bit confused. My neighbour Colm has just rung me to say a Calloway Arc van turned up with my bookcase this morning. It's Monday! I picked Thursday on purpose because I'm working away till Wednesday night, that's the whole point of the pick your day thing, I paid extra for it. Colm told the driver Thursday and the driver said fine. Then I got a text with a link to rearrange so I picked Thursday on that too. So hopefully sorted, just flagging. Also the lamp from my other order (TG-6169) came Saturday and it's gorgeous, tell whoever packs them they did a lovely job.
Thanks for your message. We aim to reply within 4 working hours. Did you know you can track every parcel in one place in the portal? This is an automated reply; please do not respond to it.
DL-90404 rebooked for Thursday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.

DL-8982 (Wrenfield TG-1750) was attempted this morning. The recipient, Quillon Larkham, says the order was placed for delivery on Thursday 9 September and that she has rearranged to Thursday through the text link. Can you confirm what date DL-8982 is booked for?

DL-8982 is on next-available service. There is no booked date on it. Attempt 1 logged failed today. A rearrangement from the text link only moves the next attempt; the route planner offers the parcel again the following morning if there is van space. We don't set booked dates, that is Whinmoor. If Whinmoor put a booked date on it, the planner drops it from earlier routes by itself and it waits at the depot. Separately, DL-2192 for the same customer was delivered Saturday, signed for.
Hi, any update on DL-75198? It was meant to come Thursday. Thanks.

He's been AGAIN. Tuesday. Colm says it was the same lad, Colm told him Thursday again and the lad said 'it just comes up on my list, mate'. Which, fair enough, not his fault. Got another text, picked Thursday again. That's twice now. Different question while I'm here, is there any way to get the cardboard taken away afterwards? The lamp box was enormous and I've nowhere to put it. Not urgent!!
Thanks for your message. We aim to reply within 4 working hours. Did you know you can track every parcel in one place in the portal? This is an automated reply; please do not respond to it.

TG-1750 / DL-8982: the customer chose Pick Your Day, Thursday 9 September, but the carrier shows next-available service with no booked date and has attempted delivery on Monday and Tuesday. What delivery date was the order sent to the carrier with?

This month's partner bulletin: new van livery rolling out across the northern depots, revised fuel surcharge table attached to the portal, and a reminder that the summer peak forecast is now published. To stop receiving these emails, update your preferences.

TG-1750: customer chose Pick Your Day, Thursday 10 Sept, at checkout. On our manifest the date went into the delivery notes text ('Deliver Thurs 10/9 only') and not into the booked-date field. It is a known fault with pick-your-day orders this month. We can't amend a manifest once the carrier has the parcel. Whinmoor at Calloway Arc can set a booked date on their side if asked. On the cardboard, we don't offer packaging take-back, sorry.
DL-21116 rebooked for Friday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.

DL-8982: 2 failed attempts. Goes out again tomorrow under next-available. Standard rule applies, a third failed attempt returns the parcel to the merchant on the next trunk. Also for your records, the customer satisfaction survey for DL-2192 has been sent to the recipient, nothing needed from you.
Route plan for depot BR-7 published for Monday. 43 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.

Route plan for depot HL-9 published for Monday. 35 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Whinmoor to put a booked date of Thursday 9 September on DL-8982 before today's 09:00-13:00 attempt, and to say whether the early attempts count toward return.

must: Asks Whinmoor to set a booked date of Thursday 9 September on DL-8982.

Gives the cause from the history: Wrenfield's Warehouse dispatch confirms the customer chose Thursday 9 September and that the date went into the delivery notes text and not the booked-date field, so the carrier has it as next-available.

Flags the urgency: it is out for delivery today between 09:00 and 13:00 with nobody at the address, this would be the third failed attempt, and a third failure returns it to the merchant. Asks whether the early attempts will count.
Tells Whinmoor that this is the third early attempt and that she has rearranged to Thursday three times through the text link without effect.
must_not: Tells the recipient to be at home, or to arrange for someone to be in, today or earlier than Thursday because the parcel is already local.
Tells the recipient to use the text link to rearrange again.
Tells the recipient that Thursday is now booked or that the parcel will not be returned, before Whinmoor confirms.
Spends the message on the cardboard take-back, the lamp order DL-2192 or the survey.
Asks Wrenfield's Warehouse dispatch to amend the manifest, which they have said they cannot do.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Urgent request on DL-8982 (Wrenfield TG-1750), which is out for delivery today between 09:00 and 13:00. Please set a booked date of Thursday 9 September on it. The customer, Quillon Larkham, chose Pick Your Day, Thursday 9 September, at checkout. Wrenfield's Warehouse dispatch confirm that on their manifest the date went into the delivery notes text ('Deliver Thurs 10/9 only') and not the booked-date field, so you have it as next-available. It was attempted on Monday and Tuesday and logged failed both times. She is working away until tonight and nobody is at the address today, so today's run would be a third failed attempt, and the depot says a third failure returns it to the merchant. Dispatch tell me a booked date takes it off earlier routes automatically. She has rearranged to Thursday three times through the text link and it has come out early each time. Could you also tell me whether the attempts made before her chosen day count toward the return limit? I have not told her Thursday is confirmed.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2705: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. 6 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
